sources.title: Meituan interview image text containing the independent A/B/C optimization problem
Structured repository question for parallelizing independent A/B/C methods
Deterministic Java validation for concurrent start, join and failure propagation

claims.text: The raw interview image text states that method a serially executes A, B and C, each takes about ten seconds, the three have no mutual dependency, and the goal is to improve execution efficiency by removing unnecessary serialization.

Java SE 21 CompletableFuture.runAsync(Runnable, Executor) runs the action asynchronously using the supplied executor; asynchronous methods without an explicit executor use CompletableFuture's default asynchronous execution facility, commonly ForkJoinPool.commonPool().

CompletableFuture.allOf completes when all supplied futures complete, and if any child completes exceptionally the aggregate future also completes exceptionally with a CompletionException carrying a cause.

The exact standalone ParallelIndependentTasks implementation is tested with a three-thread executor and a start/release latch so all three tasks must enter before any can finish; the test also verifies aggregate completion, exceptional completion, sibling execution and null guards without relying on a fragile wall-clock speed threshold.

ExecutorService exposes lifecycle methods such as shutdown; ownership determines who should close or shut down an executor, so the candidate distinguishes a locally owned example pool from container-managed/shared executors.

checks: three independent tasks can all start before a shared release gate
aggregate future waits for all normal completions
child failure propagates as exceptional aggregate completion

boundary_tests.case: three tasks blocked after concurrent start
null executor or any null task

findings: The candidate answers the source's actual optimization target by changing the dependency graph rather than discussing unrelated AQS internals.
It keeps the approximately-10-second parallel critical-path result conditional on executor capacity and absence of another shared serial bottleneck, instead of presenting it as a guaranteed SLA.
CompletableFuture runAsync/allOf and exception behavior are grounded in current Java SE 21 API documentation.
The deterministic latch test proves concurrent entry without using a flaky elapsed-time assertion and separately verifies exceptional completion.

Only the complete ParallelIndependentTasks compilation unit is marked as an auditable Java block; short caller fragments remain clearly illustrative text and no longer masquerade as standalone compilation units.
The authoritative Java block compiles standalone and matches the implementation exercised by the repository concurrency fixture.
Executor ownership and lifecycle boundaries are stated explicitly; the candidate does not prescribe per-request pool creation as production practice.
No project metric or production outcome is fabricated; required human approval remains a separate promotion gate.
